newsitem.title: UK: Over 1,000 UK gas users switch supplier daily-Ofgas.
newsitem.headline: Over 1,000 UK gas users switch supplier daily-Ofgas.

text.p: U.K. natural gas customers are leaving the former monopoly supplier in search of cheaper alternatives at the rate of over 1,000 a day, industry regulator Ofgas said on Monday.

A total of 302,823 consumers have now left British Gas Trading (BGT), formerly part of monopoly supplier British Gas plc, out of a total of 2.2 million potential customers. This represents around 14 percent of the total.

"Over a thousand customers a day are currently choosing to switch from British Gas Trading (BGT). This shows how easy it is to change gas supplier and save up to 70 sterling on your gas bill," said Clare Spottiswoode, Director General of Gas Supply.

Domestic gas competition has been introduced in phases, with Devon, Somerset and Cornwall opening up last April. A second phase followed with Avon and Dorset opening in February this year and Kent and East and West Sussex in March.
Ofgas hopes to see competition introduced in Scotland and North East England this autumn, and to the rest of the country by April 1998.

But John Battle, energy minister at the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), has said that the government will not necessarily be tied to the timetable, produced in March under the Conservative administration.
So far 104,830 customers in the first phase and 197,993 in the second phase have switched, Ofgas said.
